editorial_notice: AI-authored prepared learning material. Synthetic audio is a model for practice, not a native-speaker assessment. Introduced does not mean mastered.

episodes.title: Two letters, two sounds
episodes.goal: Meet А and М, try two sound patterns, and hear yes/no.

steps.instruction: Russian uses a different alphabet. We will connect two letters to sounds. Play this vowel, then continue.

action.note: Use the recording as your model. An English cue is the open vowel in “father” for many speakers; accents differ. Replay whenever you like.

steps.instruction: Play this syllable. Listen to its beginning, before the vowel.

action.note: М represents the beginning sound in this recording; А represents its vowel. This is a whole syllable, not a consonant letter name. Optional: imitate the beginning, then the whole example.

steps.instruction: Play the whole vowel. Which letter represents it?

options.feedback: This vowel is represented by А. Listen again, then choose А.
М represents the beginning of our other example. This whole vowel is А. Listen again.

action.success: Yes. You matched this example. Replay it whenever you like.

steps.instruction: Play the syllable. Which letter represents its beginning, before the vowel?

episodes.title: Read one real word
episodes.goal: Add О, К and Т, then build and try reading the word for cat.

steps.instruction: Listen again. Which letter represents the beginning? You may replay the introduction.

options.feedback: The beginning is represented by М. Replay ма and notice its beginning.
А is its vowel. The beginning is represented by М. Replay ма.

action.success: Yes. You matched this example. Replay it whenever you like.

steps.instruction: Play this vowel and notice its round sound.

action.note: О has this sound in this stressed example. Its sound can change in other words; that is for a later encounter.

steps.instruction: Play the syllable. Listen to its beginning, before the vowel.

action.note: К represents the beginning of ка. The recording includes the vowel; it is not an isolated consonant.

steps.instruction: Play the syllable. Listen to its beginning, before the vowel.

action.note: Т represents the beginning of та. Replay the whole syllable; optional imitation is welcome.

steps.instruction: This word means “cat”. Play the whole word and follow к → о → т.

action.note: The whole recording models the word. The three letters are already introduced.

steps.instruction: Build the word meaning “cat”. Replay the word whenever you like.

feedback: The first letter is К. Listen to the beginning of the cat word.
The middle letter is О. Replay the vowel in the cat word.
The last letter is Т. Listen to the end of the cat word.
action.success: You assembled it. Listen once more if you like.

steps.instruction: Try reading this aloud or quietly. Then reveal the model and compare. You can skip this attempt.

action.note: Listen, try, and compare at your own pace. If recording is available, you can record yourself and listen back. You can also skip this.

action.summary: You practiced А, М, О, К, Т and кот, meaning cat. Repeat the word or continue to a small message.

episodes.title: Send a small message
episodes.goal: Add Д and describe a cat at a distant location.

steps.instruction: Try reading this aloud or quietly. Then reveal the model and compare. You can skip this attempt.

action.note: Listen and compare with your attempt. What sounds different? Replay as often as you like.

steps.instruction: Play the familiar “yes” chunk. Listen to its beginning before the vowel.

action.note: Д represents the beginning of да. You have heard this whole chunk before; now both its written letters have been introduced.

steps.instruction: The spelling of the “yes” chunk is now available to read.

action.note: This is the same yes chunk. The no chunk remains listening practice; its letters are for later.

steps.instruction: Scene: you stand in a doorway. The cat sits across the room under the far window. This word means “there”: that distant spot.

action.note: In this scene, there means the spot under the far window where the cat sits.

steps.instruction: Scene: you stand in a doorway; the cat sits across the room under the far window. Describe it: “There is a cat there.” Listen and follow the two words.

action.note: Там means there; кот means cat. A space separates the words. The first letter is capitalized; the period ends the message. This Russian message needs no separate word for “is”.

steps.instruction: You stand in a doorway. The cat sits across the room under the far window. Assemble “There is a cat there.”
steps.display: Scene: you are at the doorway. The cat is across the room under the far window.

feedback: Start with Там, meaning there: the spot under the far window. Replay the message and choose that first word.
Next use кот., meaning cat, with the period ending this message. Replay the second word.
action.success: You assembled it. Listen once more if you like.

steps.instruction: Optional: build the word meaning “there”. You can replay it whenever you like.

feedback: Begin with Т; replay the beginning.
The middle letter is А; replay the vowel.
Finish with М; listen to the end.
action.success: You assembled it. Listen once more if you like.

steps.instruction: Try reading this aloud or quietly. Then reveal the model and compare. You can skip this attempt.

action.note: Listen and compare with your attempt. What sounds different? Replay as often as you like.

steps.instruction: Listen to the whole word. Which meaning did it have in our scene?

options.feedback: This is там: there, at the indicated spot. Replay it.
The cat word is different. This is там: there, at the indicated spot. Replay it.

action.success: Yes. You matched this example. Replay it whenever you like.

steps.instruction: Optional: say the small message and compare with its reference.

action.note: Listen, try, and compare at your own pace. If recording is available, you can record yourself and listen back. You can also skip this.

steps.instruction: Repeat, pause, or continue with more sound and script practice.

episodes.title: I and you, by ear
episodes.goal: Hear two useful words for taking part yourself.

steps.instruction: When you refer to yourself, the speaker, this whole word means “I”. Play it.

action.note: Its new letter has not been introduced. Learn the spoken chunk and meaning now; no Russian script is required.

steps.instruction: You are speaking to one close friend. Play the whole Russian word meaning “you” for that friend.

action.note: This word addresses one familiar person. Russian has another form for more formal address or more than one listener; that will come later. Its new written letter has not been introduced, so this is listening and speaking only.

steps.instruction: Listen. Does this word refer to the speaker or to the familiar listener? Answer in English without looking at Russian spelling.

feedback.feedback: This chunk means I, the speaker. The familiar-listener chunk is different; replay this one first.

action.reveal: This chunk means I: the person speaking.

steps.instruction: You are talking directly to one close friend. What Russian word means “you” in that scene? Try saying it before listening.

feedback.feedback: The I chunk refers to the speaker. Here you address your familiar listener. Listen to the familiar-listener reference.

action.reveal: For this familiar one-person scene, listen to the reference chunk and compare with your attempt.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You heard I and familiar you. Keep practicing them by ear while we meet more letters.

episodes.title: He and she, one letter at a time
episodes.goal: Meet one new consonant, hear two useful words, and notice which part of a word is stressed.

steps.instruction: What does this written word mean? Give its English meaning before revealing the recording.
Play this practice syllable. Notice its beginning, before the vowel.

action.note: Н looks like English H, but its beginning sound here is like the beginning of English “no”. Follow the recording. The vowel А was introduced earlier. This syllable is practice, not new vocabulary.

steps.instruction: Build the displayed syllable, then listen as you follow its letters.

feedback: Start with Н, the beginning before the vowel.
action.success: You assembled it. Replay as you follow the letters.

steps.instruction: In this scene we are talking about one man. Play the Russian word meaning “he”.

action.note: Listen to the whole word. Russian writing will appear next; no reading is needed here.

steps.instruction: This is the word you just heard. Listen, then follow its letters.

action.note: О carries the word’s vowel. Н is at the end; listen to that ending in the whole recording. The capital version is Он; both shapes of each letter have been introduced.

steps.instruction: Now we are talking about one woman. Play the Russian word meaning “she”.

action.note: This is a whole spoken word. Listen before looking at its spelling.

steps.instruction: Play the word for “she”. Notice that its final vowel is stronger.

action.note: The last syllable is stressed: stronger. The accent marks it for learning; ordinary spelling is она. The first о is unstressed, so it sounds different from our earlier stressed о. Listen to the whole word.

steps.instruction: What does this written word mean? Give its English meaning before revealing the recording.

feedback.feedback: он was he. This word has the ending а: она, she.

action.reveal: она means she in our one-woman scene. Listen and compare.

steps.instruction: Try reading this aloud or quietly, then show the model to compare. You can skip.

action.note: Listen and compare. What sounds different? You can replay and try again.

steps.instruction: Listen. In our people scenes, what does this word mean? Say or type its English meaning.

feedback.feedback: The word you heard is он, he. The word for she in our other scene ends in а: она.

action.reveal: This is он: he, referring to the man in our scene.

steps.instruction: We are talking about the woman, not the speaker or listener. What Russian word means “she”? Try saying it before listening.

feedback.feedback: он refers to the man in our first scene. For the woman, the reference is она́.

action.reveal: The reference is она́. Listen, then compare with your attempt.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You met Н and practiced he and she. You also noticed a stronger syllable and an unstressed О in one word.

episodes.title: A window, and one kind of “it”
episodes.goal: Read a new noun, then refer back to it with the Russian neuter pronoun.

steps.instruction: Scene: a cat sits beside a window. Play the Russian word for the window.

action.note: Play the example, then continue when you are ready.

steps.instruction: Play the whole window word. Follow its four letters.

action.note: The last о is stressed; the first is unstressed, as in она́. Hear К and Н together, without an extra vowel. Follow the whole word. Ordinary spelling is окно.

steps.instruction: We have just named the window. Play the pronoun that can refer back to that window.

action.note: The Russian word for window is a neuter noun. This pronoun can refer back to it. Other noun classes use different pronouns; this is the window example.

steps.instruction: Listen, then follow the spelling of the pronoun for our window.

action.note: The last о is stressed; the first is unstressed. Listen to the whole word. Ordinary spelling is оно.

steps.instruction: Listen to the pronoun for our window noun. Keep this particular example in mind.

action.note: Окно, window, is a neuter noun. Оно can refer back to it. Russian uses different pronouns for different noun classes; this is the window example.

steps.instruction: Return to the man in our earlier scene. What Russian word means “he”? Say it before revealing the model.

feedback.feedback: она refers to the woman in our scene. For the man, use он.
оно was used for the neuter window noun. For the man in this scene, use он.

steps.instruction: The letter keys enter your answer. Backspace removes the last letter. Next, try copying a short word with these keys.

action.note: The Russian word stays visible for this first keyboard try. If tapping is difficult, you can ask for help or skip.

steps.instruction: Try this input control: tap О, then Н. Backspace removes the last letter.

action.note: The same keys will be available for other words. Backspace removes the last letter. You can use a spoken answer or skip whenever typing is awkward.

steps.instruction: Enter the Russian word for “window” from memory. Use the letter keyboard, or ask for help. The word and recording appear after your answer.

feedback.feedback: оно is the pronoun used for the window noun. The noun meaning window is окно: it includes К.

action.reveal: The spelling is окно. Replay окно́ and follow О К Н О.

steps.instruction: What does this written word mean? Give its English meaning before revealing the recording.

feedback.feedback: The noun is window. The separate pronoun for this neuter noun was оно, without К.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You practiced окно, window, and оно referring back to that neuter noun. Next comes a word for more than one person.

episodes.title: They: more than one person
episodes.goal: Meet one new vowel and hear how the consonant before it sounds in this word.

steps.instruction: Play this vowel and connect it with these letter shapes.

action.note: The recording is the model. For many English speakers the vowel in “see” is a useful starting cue, though accents differ. И is a Russian letter; it is not the English letter N.

steps.instruction: Now two people stand together: the man and the woman. Play the Russian word meaning “they”.

action.note: Play the example, then continue when you are ready.

steps.instruction: Play the whole word. Notice its final vowel and the sound just before it.

action.note: The last syllable is stressed. The first о is unstressed, as before. Н sounds softer before и here than at the end of он. Follow the whole word; we will explore that difference later. Ordinary spelling is они.

steps.instruction: What does this written word mean? Give its English meaning before revealing the recording.

feedback.feedback: он refers to the one man. This word ends in И: они, they.
она refers to the one woman. This word ends in И: они, they.

action.reveal: они means they, referring to the two people together in our scene.

steps.instruction: Try reading this aloud or quietly, then show the model to compare. You can skip.

action.note: Listen and compare. What sounds different? You can replay and try again.

steps.instruction: What Russian word means “she” for the woman in our scene? Enter it before revealing its spelling or recording.

feedback.feedback: он was he. For she in our scene, add the final А: она.
они was they, for more than one person. Our one-woman word ends in А: она.

action.reveal: The spelling is она. Listen to она́.

steps.instruction: Listen without looking at the Russian spelling. In our people scenes, what does this word mean?

feedback.feedback: The recording is они, ending in И, for the two people. The one-man word was он.
The recording is они, ending in И, for the two people. The one-woman word was она.

action.reveal: This is они: they, the two people together.

steps.instruction: We named the window in Russian. Say the pronoun that refers back to this neuter noun, then reveal the model.

feedback.feedback: In this taught example, окно is neuter, so use оно. он was our word for the man.
In this taught example, окно is neuter, so use оно. она was our word for the woman.

action.reveal: For the neuter noun окно, the pronoun is оно́.

steps.instruction: Back to our two people together. What Russian word means “they”? Try saying it before listening.

feedback.feedback: он was one man. For both people together, the reference is они́.
она was one woman. For both people together, the reference is они́.

steps.instruction: Pause, repeat, or continue.

action.summary: You practiced И, they, and returns to earlier words. Continue with small new letter encounters and useful short exchanges.
